children: HSBC Holdings PLC Sponsored ADR (LSE:HSBA) boosted shareholder returns with a second interim dividend and sizable buybacks while trimming non-core revenue and targeting $2B of simplification savings, even as it leans into Hong Kong, wealth flows and Gift City deposits amid CFO Pam Kaur’s planned exit.
: HSBC (HSBA) declared a second interim 2026 dividend of $0.10 per ordinary share, payable Sept 25, 2026 to holders of record Aug 14, 2026. ADSs get $0.50 each.
Wealth Growth Led By Hong Kong
: HSBC ADR (HSBA): Hong Kong and wealth management drive growth. Hong Kong ROE about 45% (unconstrained); leverage could cut ROE to 30%+. Q2 wealth net new money $22B, ~8% annualized growth.
: HSBC ADR (HSBA) repurchased shares Sept 11–16: total buys include 1.204M HKEX shares (~HK$194.1M) and 5.8M on other exchanges (~£87.7M), across multiple transactions.
: HSBC Holdings ADR (HSBA): exits since 2025 cut about $2B revenue, ~$1.1B exit costs. Current-year impact ~1/3 of total, rising to ~3/4 next year; simplification savings target $2B.
: HSBC (HSBA): CFO Pam Kaur to leave after 13 years; bank to target growth with cost discipline, four focus businesses, and set minimum targets to guide management and handover.
: HSBC Holdings ADR (HSBA) supplied $10.9B of $52.8B lent via Gift City. FCNR deposits come from 30+ markets, target Indian NRIs; deposit range $100k–$2.5M, rates up to 5.5%.
: HSBC Holdings (HSBA) raised its US dollar savings rate to 0.125% and kept Hong Kong dollar best lending rate at 5.00%, with HKD savings rates unchanged.
: HSBC Holdings PLC Sponsored ADR (HSBA) is an anchor investor in the upcoming NSE IPO, joining other institutional backers in the anchor allocation and forming part of the initial investor base.
